subject: humanities
passage: Music teacher Joseph Mensah teaches some of his students new songs by playing each song aloud and having them copy what they hear. He teaches his other students the same songs from written sheet music. Mensah hypothesizes that students who learn a song by ear remember it longer than students who learn it from sheet music.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Mensah's hypothesis?

choices.A: Students who learned from sheet music needed fewer lessons to learn each song than the other students did.
choices.B: Months after the lessons, both groups of students could play about the same number of songs from memory.
choices.C: Most of Mensah's students said they enjoyed learning by ear more than learning from sheet music.
choices.D: Months after the lessons, students who had learned by ear could play more of the songs from memory.

explanation.why: Mensah's hypothesis is about memory over time: learning by ear should help students remember songs longer. Support must show the by-ear group remembering more of the songs after time has passed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This is about how quickly songs were learned, not how long they were remembered.
explanation.B: Incorrect. If both groups remembered equally, learning by ear would show no advantage; this weakens the hypothesis.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Enjoying a method is different from remembering songs longer because of it.
explanation.D: Correct. After months, the by-ear students remembered more songs, which is what Mensah predicts.
